structured_output.title: Quiet day: no NGC2 movement, one thin Anduril data point
structured_output.dek: Nothing today rose above background — the only item touching the thesis is a passing confirmation that Lattice sits inside the Army's counter-drone C2 layer.

sections.heading: Nothing moved on the programs that matter
sections.markdown:
No coverage today of Next Generation Command and Control, Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node, Program Executive Office Command Control Communications and Network, Program Executive Office Intelligence Electronic Warfare and Sensors, or Defense Innovation Unit solicitations. No architecture decisions, no awards, no protests in that portfolio.

A quiet day is worth recording as such. Nothing in the day's traffic either supports or undermines the on-platform inference bet.

sections.heading: The one competitive data point
sections.markdown:
A United States Army sources-sought notice for a sub-$150K counter-drone interceptor — Group 2 and Group 3 targets, greater than 16km at 6km altitude, responses due Aug. 20 — restates in passing that Anduril Industries was picked to supply Lattice for the IBCS-M program. The missile itself is irrelevant here; the reminder that Lattice holds the C2 slot in Army counter-drone architecture is not.

The new munition would have to be compatible with the Coyote launcher, which RTX holds under a $5 billion award, and with IBCS-M. Read that as Anduril Industries accreting integration surface in a mission area where sensor-to-shooter timelines make on-platform processing a natural requirement. Nothing in the notice specifies where detection and track inference actually runs — that is what would resolve whether this is an edge slot or a networked one.

Anduril Industries also appears, alongside SMARTSHOOTER, DroneShield and Aerovironment, as a catalogue vendor on a new counter-drone procurement marketplace. That is shelf space, not a technical win.

sections.heading: Acquisition mechanics, filed for pattern
sections.markdown:
Two items are only interesting as procedure. A Pentagon counter-drone task force awarded a four-year-old software firm $15M via other transaction agreement in May to prototype a counter-UAS marketplace, now live with Australia, Poland, Republic of Korea, Romania and the United Kingdom onboarded. The vendor's CEO uses "deployed at the edge" to mean acquisition speed, not inference location — discount it entirely.

Separately, a General Dynamics protest against a sole-source award to Leidos for combatant-command network migration was dismissed after the agency reopened the work to market research, with a ~220-day competitive cycle now estimated against a September 2028 deadline. Two takeaways: a protest successfully converted a sole-source into a competition, and the underlying direction is consolidating 231,000 users across 200 sites into a single managed enterprise architecture. The second is a mild centralization counter-signal, though it concerns back-office IT rather than sensor processing.

sections.heading: Background noise
sections.markdown:
United States Space Force issued $615M in other transaction agreements to three vendors for space-based airborne moving target indicator work, following a $4.16B award in May, explicitly to avoid lock-in to a single technical solution. No edge-versus-downlink claims in the announcement — which is itself the gap worth watching, since AMTI from orbit is exactly where sensor volume outruns downlink.

United States Navy renewed a $16.3M task order for maritime USV counter-narcotics patrols in SOUTHCOM into 2027. Autonomy spend, no inference architecture disclosed.
